variant_a.facts: In your letter dated August 20, 2026, you requested a country of origin ruling on a windchime for purposes of current trade remedies. The product under consideration is a windchime identified as the RS 31.5in metal chicken windchime, which measures approximately 31.5 inches in height and 8 inches in diameter. Each windchime consists of a dome-shaped metal top piece with metal tubes, flowers, roosters, a clapper, and a flower windcatcher suspended beneath. Three metal chains are connected to a hook at the top of the dome for hanging. In your ruling request submission and subsequent email correspondence, you state that the windchimes are assembled in Vietnam using components sourced from both China and Vietnam. The components sourced from China include the top pieces, flowers, rooster bodies, clappers, and windcatchers. The components of Vietnamese origin are the rooster wings and tubes. The factory combines these Vietnamese-origin components with the Chinese-origin parts to create the finished windchimes. The assembly process in Vietnam begins by welding the imported components. Specifically, the factory in Vietnam welds the Chinese-origin rooster bodies and the Vietnamese-origin wings together to form complete roosters. These roosters are then combined with the other imported components and the Vietnamese-made metal tubes (chimes) to assemble the finished windchime. This manufacturing process includes spot welding, polishing, powder coating, paint spraying, and hand-painting (using coating and paint of Vietnamese origin). Finally, the finished products undergo testing and inspection before being packaged for export. The Bill of Materials (BOM) demonstrates that the manufacturing operations in Vietnam contribute approximately 31% of the total cost of production and final value of the windchimes.

variant_a.facts: 2026, you requested a country of origin ruling on an automotive air filter. Descriptive literature was provided for our review. The item under consideration is described as an automotive air filter (model WT214037), which is a component of an automotive heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system designed to clean the air entering the vehicle’s interior. The device filters out dust, pollen, mold, bacteria, and other airborne particles, improving the air quality inside the car. The filter is usually located behind the glove compartment or under the dashboard. The filter includes a polypropylene (PP) frame, pleated filter media, and a rubber seal gasket. The air filter is assembled in Thailand using components sourced from China and Thailand. The Chinese components include the filter media (pleated paper), rubber seal, color box, and labels. The Thai components include plastic pellets (used for the PP frame), blank outer boxes, fumigated solid wood pallets, cardboard, and paper angle beads. The assembly and manufacturing process occurs entirely in Thailand and includes multiple sequential steps across specialized equipment. The process begins with non-woven fabric slitting, followed by folding line pressing, media pleating, and media slitting. Subsequently, the paper block is placed into the manufacturing line, followed by PP vertical injection molding to form the PP frame, assembling the sealing ring, spraying data code via an inkjet printer/laser marker, plastic packing using a laminating machine, and final packaging.

variant_a.facts: In your letter dated January 15, 2026, on behalf of your client, Jiangmen Lingfeng Electric Appliances Manufacturing Co., Ltd., you requested a country of origin ruling on four models of electric heaters for purposes of marking and applying current trade remedies. The merchandise under consideration is referred to as “Plastic Heater”, “Metal Heater”, “Stove Heater”, and “Salamander Heater” (the “heaters”). Each of the four heater models is designed for use in household, commercial or industrial environments to provide directed thermal output. All products incorporate a heating element, an electric motor, a fan to distribute heated air, structural housing (either plastic or metal), and electrical hardware such as wiring, switches, and connectors. Additionally, the Stove Heater model contains a printed circuit board (PCB). You state that the heating elements and PCBs are manufactured in Thailand using calibrated resistance wire and integrated thermal control mechanisms. The balance of components referenced above will be made in China. These heating elements and PBCs are shipped as prefabricated components to China, where they are mechanically installed into each unit with the Chinese-made components without any alteration or reprocessing. The Chinese operations include final mechanical assembly, electrical wiring, mounting of the fan and motor, installation of the housing, and packaging of the completed unit for export. You further state that these heating elements and PCBs are simply installed using fasteners and electrical connections during the final assembly in China.

In your letter dated September 23, 2026, on behalf of your client, Jiangmen Lingfeng Electric Appliances Manufacturing Co., Ltd., you requested a country of origin ruling on electric stove heaters for purposes of applying current trade remedies. The merchandise under consideration is referred to as Electric Stove Heater Model H3D-B15 (the “Stove Heater”). Model H3D-B15 is an electric stove heater designed to provide heated airflow while presenting the appearance of a traditional stove/fireplace through a decorative illuminated log assembly. The heating function is produced through the coordinated operation of a resistance heating element, electric motor, and wind-turbine/fan assembly. The heating element generates heat, while the motor drives the wind-turbine assembly to move air through the heating system and distribute the heated airflow. The Thailand-manufactured PCBA provides the appliance's electronic control functions, including temperature and heating control, fan interlock, user-interface functions, safety monitoring and protection, flame-effect control, and power management. These functional components are incorporated into a fabricated metal housing together with the front door, decorative illuminated log assembly, wiring, safety components, and related hardware. The Stove Heater is manufactured in Thailand from components and materials originating in Thailand, Vietnam, and China. The resistance heating element is manufactured in Vietnam. In Thailand, however, significant motor manufacturing and assembly occur; the heating element is incorporated into the heating system and integrated with the motor and wind-turbine assembly; the metal housing is fabricated; and the various electrical, structural, heating, and decorative components are assembled into the finished appliance. The completed Stove Heater is also tested and inspected in Thailand. You describe the manufacturing process in Thailand as follows:
A. Motor Manufacturing The motor is not imported into Thailand as a completed foreign-origin motor. In Thailand, lacquered wire and related inputs are used to manufacture the coil assembly through coil winding and wiring, lead-wire preparation and soldering, insulation, and performance testing. The completed coil assembly is then inserted into a China-origin stator. A China-origin rotor with shaft and gear housing are subsequently assembled with the stator/coil assembly, and the motor components are fastened together. The completed motor undergoes electrical and performance testing in Thailand, including hi-pot, noise, current, leakage-current, and low-voltage startup testing. Thus, although the stator and rotor with shaft originate in China, significant motor manufacturing and assembly operations occur in Thailand before the motor is incorporated into the Stove Heater. B. Heating and Wind-Turbine Assembly The resistance heating element itself is manufactured in Vietnam and shipped to Thailand. The completed heating assembly is not manufactured in Vietnam. In Thailand, the imported heating element is installed into the heating box to form the heating assembly. That assembly is then installed into the wind-turbine assembly, and the motor is incorporated into the combined heating and airflow system. The resulting assembly undergoes performance testing and inspection in Thailand. Thus, although the resistance heating element originates in Vietnam, the complete forced-air heating system is created through the integration of the heating element, motor, and wind-turbine assembly in Thailand. C. Metal Housing and Final Assembly The metal housing is fabricated in Thailand from coated sheet through multiple punching, trimming, deburring, hemming, bending, and forming operations. The functional and structural systems are then integrated into the finished Stove Heater in Thailand. The Thai operations include assembly of the housing, switches and circuit board, installation of the heating/motor/wind-turbine system, assembly of the front door and rear board, and final product integration. The finished unit undergoes aging, performance testing, appearance inspection, packaging, and storage in Thailand. The remaining identified China-origin components include the power cord, switch, lead wires, flame-effect lighting assembly, screws, and nuts.

verification: Read both. Same requester (named in both facts), same Stove Heater type. A: Thai heating element and PCB fitted in China with Chinese motor, fan and housing, held China. B: motor coil made, housing fabricated, heating system built and unit assembled in Thailand, held Thailand. Several groups move at once.
notes: A covers four heater models; the Stove Heater is one.

variant_a.facts: In your letter dated November 13, 2025, you requested a country of origin ruling. The item under consideration is Strut Assembly, Model Number S0099-A0330, which is used in passenger vehicles. You state that the main function of the strut assembly is to provide damping support to a vehicle's suspension system. The strut assembly consists of a shock absorber, strut mount, upper spring bumper, and upper spring seat from Thailand, and a coil spring, bumper stop, and strut dust shield from China. The shock absorber consists of a tube, connecting rod (piston), and lubricating oil from China, and spring seat, bottom cover, and lugs from Thailand. In Thailand, the components of the shock absorber are assembled into a complete shock absorber. The shock absorber is then inserted into the coil spring and combined with the rest of the components.

variant_b.facts:
In your letter dated September 4, 2026, you requested a country of origin ruling on a complete strut assembly on behalf of your client Jinbo Auto Parts (Thailand) Co., Ltd. The article under consideration is a complete strut assembly (CSA), Part Number S0143-A0011, designed for use on Ford-150 (2004-2008) and Lincoln Mark LT (2006-2008). The CSA is a primary automotive suspension component, combining a coil spring and a shock absorber (strut) into a single integrated unit. It is installed on the front axle of vehicles with independent suspension setups. Its function is to bear vehicle weight, absorb vertical road impacts and vibrations, maintain tire contact with the road surface, and provide vehicle stability and passenger comfort. The CSA consists of a coil spring, strut, mounts, bumpers, and dust cover. The manufacturing processes and final assembly occurs in Thailand. In Thailand, the raw material and purchased components from China are received and inspected. The bottom cover is press-fitted onto the outer/reservoir tube using a high-precision press machine, followed by press forming to the required dimensions, and welded. The welded assemblies undergo 100% leak testing to detect microscopic weld failures. Following the assembly, the inner walls of the tubes undergo multi-stage ultrasonic cleaning to remove all particles and contaminants. The completed outer reservoir tube is assembled with related housing components to form the reservoir tube sub-assembly. The base valve assembly is a sub-assembly comprising multiple discs, washers, valves, seals, and rings assembled and riveted together in a precise sequence. The piston rod, manufactured from raw round steel through CNC machining, tapping, drilling, boring, and grinding, is assembled with multiple components to create a functional piston rod assembly: A rebound limit ring is precision-welded to the piston rod. The welded rod undergoes multi-stage ultrasonic cleaning to remove weld residue and particles that could damage seals. The loading guider sub-assembly is pressed onto the piston rod. The oil seal is lubricated and installed onto the rod.
The rod valve pack is assembled onto the rod following the same critical sequencing as the base valve assembly. A specialty locking nut is torqued to a precise specification; incorrect torque results in poor damping performance and testing failure. Nuts are punch-deformed to permanently secure the valve pack and prevent slippage. The piston rod is transformed from a machined steel rod into a functional suspension sub-assembly through welding, cleaning, assembly, torquing, and locking. The reservoir tube sub-assembly is filled with precisely specified absorber oil using an automated oil injection machine, and the piston rod assembly is inserted. Oil specification is critical to damping performance: different viscosity grades affect compression and rebound response, temperature tolerance, and seal longevity. After oil filling, the guide is pre-tightened to set the correct compression force on the oil seal. The assembled unit then undergoes 100% damping force testing to verify performance against specifications. The outer tube is then sealed by flanging, permanently enclosing the internal assembly. Finally, nitrogen is charged into the sealed unit. Nitrogen charging prevents hydraulic fluid foaming, resulting in more consistent and durable suspension control. The result is a completed bare shock absorber. The completed bare shock absorber is loaded onto an automated painting line, spray-painted for corrosion protection and finishing. Following that, the dust cover and dust shield are installed to protect the piston rod. Then, the anti-collision pad is installed to buffer at maximum compression, followed by the ring and ring bushing. Finally, the coil spring and upper/lower spring bumpers are installed using a coil spring press machine, and the strut mount and spring disc are installed and secured with top nuts torqued to specification. The finished CSA is labeled and packaged per customer specifications, and the finished goods are then transferred to inventory for shipment.

difference: Shock absorber made in Thailand from raw steel and sub-parts (piston rod machined, reservoir tube welded, valves built, oil filled, nitrogen charged) instead of assembled from a Chinese tube, piston rod and oil.
verification: Read both. Same product type and part-number scheme (S0099 / S0143), strut assembled in Thailand in both. A: shock absorber tube, piston rod and oil from China, held China (the shock absorber). B: shock absorber made in Thailand, held Thailand.
notes: Different requester names; same Thai assembly pattern.

variant_a.facts:
In your letter dated September 22, 2026, you requested a country of origin ruling on behalf of your client, Jereh Energy Equipment and Technologies Corporation for the purpose of marking, Section 301 Trade Remedies, and other duties. The products at issue are referred to as Trailer Mounted Intelligent Electrical Fracking (TMEF) Units, model numbers YLT105-5600E, YLT95-5600E, and YLT105-6000E. Each unit is a trailer equipped with an electrically powered Quintuplex Plunger Pump assembly, a power assembly, high- and low-pressure assemblies, a lubrication system, a power-end lubrication assembly, a medium-voltage drive assembly, a variable-frequency drive assembly, an electrical cabinet and a control assembly. Once powered by an electric grid or a Power2Go gas turbine generator set, these assemblies work together to pump various types of fluids used for oil and gas fracturing operations. The TMEF units are differentiated by their temperature thresholds, working pressures and power output. The plunger pump assembly consists of a Quintuplex plunger pump (power and fluid ends and a reducer), a return oil pipe and a cover plate assembly. The pump, which is configured as a reciprocating positive displacement pump pressurizes the low and medium pressure water supplies and then delivers the water through a designated manifold. The power assembly consists of an oil cooler pre-assembly, a drive shaft, a medium-voltage motor and other power assembly components. Its function is to transmit power from the motor to the plunger pump via a drive shaft. The high-pressure assembly consists of a pressure sensor, a hose bracket, a wing nut and a male plug. The low-pressure assembly consists of lubrication pipe, cast manifold, hose bracket, an accumulator and a u-type liquid inlet. Together, the components convey the low-pressure water supply to the plunger pump.
The packing lubrication assembly consists of a lubrication pump and hose connections. The function of the assembly is to lubricate the five-way packing of the plunger pump. The power-end lubrication assembly is driven by a motor that powers two double pumps, which provide lubrication for the bearings and gears inside the power end of the plunger pump. The gear pumps suction lube oil from the oil tank through suction oil filters and then deliver oil to the plunger pump via pipelines. The medium voltage drive assembly is used for electrical frequency conversion and voltage transformation to satisfy the needs of power supply scenarios. The variable frequency drive assembly consists of five outdoor units that are used to control the actuation and speed control of the lubrication motor. The electrical cabinet houses all electrical controls for the TMEF unit, including sensors, sensor cables, main motor power cables, lubrication motor power cables and other components. The control assembly is a centralized point of access for all electrical equipment and protection of equipment safety. New York Rulings N357930 and N360430, dated February 18, 2026, and April 24, 2026, respectively, previously addressed the country of origin for this product, which underwent final assembly in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). This submission provides additional details on the assembly process and updates the origin of certain components. With regard to origin, each TMEF unit is assembled in the UAE. The final assembly process involves installing the main assemblies either in their complete manner or as individual components onto a trailer, all of which are sourced from China. The only exceptions to this Chinese sourcing are the drive shaft, which comes from Germany, and the plunger pump, which is sourced from the UAE. Prior to final assembly, the components of these main assemblies undergo sandblasting and painting. During final assembly, components such as cable clips, clamps, cable trays, grounding posts, base plates, latches, hinges, reinforced sleeves, fastening plates, brackets, fenders, and ladder brackets, all sourced from China, are fitted and welded onto the trailer. Next, the main assemblies are mounted and secured onto the trailer using bolts and screws, either as complete units or as individual components. As needed, an anti-adhesion agent is applied, cylindrical pins are positioned, and grease is applied. Once all assemblies and their individual components are secured, clamp connections and connecting pipes, also sourced from China, are attached to the various assemblies, and all electrical connections are completed. Each TMEF unit undergoes testing. Finally, each TMEF unit is covered with a tarpaulin and secured using straps.

product: Pneumatic wrench (1/2-inch drive), same Malaysian plant

variant_a.facts:
In your letter dated October 1, 2026, you requested a country of origin ruling on a pneumatic ratchet wrench. Product information was submitted with your request. The item under consideration is a pneumatic ratchet wrench (Item number 1151200011) to tighten and loosen nuts and bolts for automotive and industrial assembly work. The ratchet wrench features a 1/2-inch square drive anvil, single ratchet pawl head, reversible direction, and quick connect plug. You state that the ratchet wrench is capable of delivering 150 rotations per minute (free speed) and a max torque of 61 Newton-meters (45 foot-pounds). During operation, the user applies pressure to the lever which allows compressed air to enter the tool. The compressed air is precisely channeled by the cylinder housing to push against rotor vanes. This action provides the primary rotational power which is transferred to the wrench’s anvil. The single-pawl ratchet mechanism allows for rotation in one direction while preventing motion in the reverse direction. As you described, the ratchet wrench is assembled in Malaysia from Malaysian and Chinese components. In Malaysia, rough metal blanks and bar stock from China undergoes CNC machining such as drilling, threading, turning, boring, grinding, and deburring to obtain the form of the finished cylinder housing, ratchet housing, and quick-connect plug. With regard to the wrench housing, aluminum ingots sourced from Malaysia are die-cast to shape prior to CNC machining. These processes deliver the precise shapes, dimensions, drilled holes, threading, and surfaces which the components rely on for functioning. All Malaysian-manufactured parts undergo testing for performance and inspection for quality.
Additionally, several Chinese-origin components are imported to Malaysia ready for assembly without further processing. These components include, but are not limited to, the rotor, the rotor vanes, the ratchet anvil assembly, the ratchet yoke, the crank shaft, the valve stem, valve plugs, end plates, bearings, and gears. Final assembly of the ratchet wrench begins with the installation of the valve seat fitting and valve plug onto the wrench housing. After that, the rear bearing is installed to the rear end plate. The rear end plate, rotor vanes, cylinder housing, front end plate, and front bearing are installed into and onto the rotor. Following that, the cylinder housing containing the rotor and other components is installed into the housing. A ring gear is then installed onto the housing, and an idler gear is installed onto the idler gear shaft. At that point, the idler gear shaft, clamp nut, and ratchet housing are installed onto the wrench housing. The drive bushing is installed onto the crank shaft which is installed into the rachet housing. In the next steps, the ratchet yoke and ratchet anvil assembly are assembled onto the ratchet housing. Assembly finishes with the installation of the lever, pin, and air inlet with quick-connect plug onto the wrench housing. Finally, the completed ratchet wrench is tested for function and accuracy and packed in a box for export to the United States.

In your letter dated October 1, 2026, you requested a country of origin ruling on a pneumatic impact wrench. Product information was submitted with your request. The item under consideration is a pneumatic impact wrench (Item Number 1151200001) to tighten and loosen nuts and bolts for automobile tire maintenance and industrial assembly. The impact wrench features a 1/2-inch square drive anvil, twin hammer impact mechanism, reversible direction, and a quick-connect plug. You state that the impact wrench is capable of delivering up to 1000 foot-pounds of torque. During operation, the user applies pressure to the trigger which allows compressed air to enter the tool. The compressed air pushes against rotor blades which forces the rotor to spin at high speeds. This action provides the primary rotational power which is transferred to the wrench’s anvil. As the wrench encounters resistance from a nut or bolt, its hammer mechanism strikes the anvil with powerful impacts to increase torque output and overcome the resistance. As you described, the impact wrench is assembled in Malaysia from Malaysian and Chinese components. In Malaysia, rough metal blanks from China undergo CNC machining such as milling, drilling, boring, grinding, grooving, and deburring to obtain the form of the finished anvil, hammer cage, cylinder, and rotor. These processes deliver the precise shapes, dimensions, splining, drilled holes, slots, and surfaces which the components rely on for functioning. The anvil, hammer cage, and rotor also undergo heat treatment to achieve specified hardness and mechanical properties. Also in Malaysia, plastic pellets sourced from China undergo injection molding and over-molding to form the wrench’s plastic housing and grip. In your letter dated October 1, 2026, you requested a country of origin ruling on a pneumatic ratchet wrench. Product information was submitted with your request. The item under consideration is a pneumatic ratchet wrench (Item number 1151200011) to tighten and loosen nuts and bolts for automotive and industrial assembly work. The ratchet wrench features a 1/2-inch square drive anvil, single ratchet pawl head, reversible direction, and quick connect plug. You state that the ratchet wrench is capable of delivering 150 rotations per minute (free speed) and a max torque of 61 Newton-meters (45 foot-pounds). During operation, the user applies pressure to the lever which allows compressed air to enter the tool. The compressed air is precisely channeled by the cylinder housing to push against rotor vanes. This action provides the primary rotational power which is transferred to the wrench’s anvil. The single-pawl ratchet mechanism allows for rotation in one direction while preventing motion in the reverse direction. As you described, the ratchet wrench is assembled in Malaysia from Malaysian and Chinese components. In Malaysia, rough metal blanks and bar stock from China undergoes CNC machining such as drilling, threading, turning, boring, grinding, and deburring to obtain the form of the finished cylinder housing, ratchet housing, and quick-connect plug. With regard to the wrench housing, aluminum ingots sourced from Malaysia are die-cast to shape prior to CNC machining. These processes deliver the precise shapes, dimensions, drilled holes, threading, and surfaces which the components rely on for functioning. All Malaysian-manufactured parts undergo testing for performance and inspection for quality.
Additionally, several Chinese-origin components are imported to Malaysia ready for assembly without further processing. These components include, but are not limited to, the rotor, the rotor vanes, the ratchet anvil assembly, the ratchet yoke, the crank shaft, the valve stem, valve plugs, end plates, bearings, and gears. Final assembly of the ratchet wrench begins with the installation of the valve seat fitting and valve plug onto the wrench housing. After that, the rear bearing is installed to the rear end plate. The rear end plate, rotor vanes, cylinder housing, front end plate, and front bearing are installed into and onto the rotor. Following that, the cylinder housing containing the rotor and other components is installed into the housing. A ring gear is then installed onto the housing, and an idler gear is installed onto the idler gear shaft. At that point, the idler gear shaft, clamp nut, and ratchet housing are installed onto the wrench housing. The drive bushing is installed onto the crank shaft which is installed into the rachet housing. In the next steps, the ratchet yoke and ratchet anvil assembly are assembled onto the ratchet housing. Assembly finishes with the installation of the lever, pin, and air inlet with quick-connect plug onto the wrench housing. Finally, the completed ratchet wrench is tested for function and accuracy and packed in a box for export to the United States.
